content.value_statement: Production data teams need reliable patterns for pipelines, quality checks, and orchestration. This skill guides architecture, scaffolding, and DataOps practices for modern data stacks.
actual_capabilities: Explains pipeline architecture patterns for batch, streaming, and distributed processing.
Guides data modeling choices, schema design, partitioning, and quality checks.
Provides Python scaffolds for orchestration, data quality validation, and ETL performance workflows.
Covers DataOps practices for monitoring, CI/CD, logging, and incident response.
Lists operational command examples for testing, formatting, deployment, and monitoring.
limitations: The bundled Python scripts are scaffolds and do not implement complete processing logic.
It does not provision cloud infrastructure or manage secrets.
Users must verify commands before running them in production environments.
Advice must be adapted to local data contracts and governance rules.

use_cases.title: Design Reliable Pipelines
use_cases.description: Create batch or streaming pipeline plans with orchestration, validation, monitoring, and failure handling.

use_cases.title: Improve Data Models
use_cases.description: Select modeling patterns, partitioning strategies, and quality checks for analytics and machine learning datasets.

use_cases.title: Standardize DataOps
use_cases.description: Define repeatable practices for CI/CD, observability, incident response, and production operations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a daily ETL pipeline for customer events. Include ingestion, validation, transformation, storage, scheduling, and monitoring steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Data Quality Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed data pipeline and add schema checks, freshness checks, anomaly detection, alerting, and recovery actions.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Pipeline Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Spark and dbt workflow for performance risks. Recommend partitioning, caching, incremental processing, and observability improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Design a DataOps Operating Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DataOps operating model for multiple data teams. Cover CI/CD, ownership, incident response, security controls, and release governance.

output_examples.input: Design a streaming analytics pipeline for product events.
output: Architecture: producers, event broker, stream processor, lakehouse storage, and dashboard layer.
Reliability: checkpoint processing state, retry transient failures, and track event lag.
Quality: validate schema, required fields, event time, and duplicate rates.
Monitoring: alert on freshness, processing latency, error rates, and storage failures.

output_examples.input: Improve quality controls for a machine learning feature table.
output: Add freshness, null rate, range, uniqueness, and distribution checks.
Define owners for each feature group and escalation paths for failed checks.
Track quality trends over time and block downstream jobs when critical checks fail.
Document expected feature semantics and allowed value ranges.

output_examples.input: Reduce long build times in an analytics transformation project.
output: Prioritize incremental models for large fact tables and stable historical partitions.
Review join keys, table clustering, and partition filters before adding compute.
Measure model duration, warehouse cost, row counts, and source freshness.
Remove unused transformations and split expensive models into clearer stages.

best_practices: Start with explicit data contracts, ownership, and service level targets.
Validate data at ingestion, transformation, and serving boundaries.
Monitor freshness, volume, schema changes, latency, cost, and failure rates.
anti_patterns: Running production pipelines without alerting, ownership, or rollback plans.
Treating data quality checks as optional after deployment.
Embedding secrets or environment-specific assumptions in pipeline logic.

faq.question: Does this skill run data pipelines for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and scaffold scripts that users must adapt, review, and run in their own environment.

faq.question: Which data tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It references Python, SQL, Spark, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, and related DataOps tools.

faq.question: Can it help with streaming systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Kafka-style event pipelines, stream processing, checkpointing, latency monitoring, and fault tolerance.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It can draft implementation plans and scaffolds, but users must complete business logic, tests, deployment settings, and security review.

faq.question: Is it suitable for data governance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers access control, audit logging, encryption concepts, PII handling, and data quality ownership patterns.

faq.question: How should teams use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Use it to request architecture reviews, pipeline plans, quality check designs, and operational runbooks inside your chosen AI coding workflow.
